_why: ADR 0065's table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py. First entry cleared
_p2_is_not_here_on_purpose: ADR 0065's table has two rows. P2 -- 'pipeline throws a plain object
again' -- is NOT in this set, and its absence is the honest thing rather
P2 is caught by scripts/check_thrown_values_are_errors.py, not by a test.
That is the whole argument of ADR 0065: the readers were hardened too,
so reverting the throw changes no observable behaviour and no suite can
fail on it. Putting P2 in a set file would make this harness report it
NOT CAUGHT, which is true of the tests and false of the codebase --
exactly the kind of technically-accurate, materially-misleading result
this project treats as a defect.
P2 is verified by re-applying the defect verbatim and watching the guard
exit 1. That was done, and is recorded in ADR 0065.

mutations.description: describeError stops reading .message off a thrown object
mutations._note: The recovery path for a non-Error carrying a message. Without it, a plain object falls through to String(value) and renders as "[object Object]".

mutations.description: describeError returns an empty string instead of a last-resort message
mutations._note: Not in the original table. An empty `error` field reads as 'no error' -- a failure rendering as success. Added while writing this set file, because the set is meant to be runnable evidence rather than a transcript.
mutations.find: return stringified.trim() === '' ? 'An unknown error occurred (no details were recorded)' : stringified;
